overview.title: Your standards in one place
overview.body: Each card is a standard or regulation your organisation works towards. The ring shows requirement coverage: how much of the standard is documented by records you have linked, and how recent they are.
overview.step1: Enable the standards that are in scope. Start with the ones your customers or regulators ask about.
overview.step2: Open a standard to assess each requirement: mark what does not apply, and link risks, documents, suppliers or any other record as evidence.
overview.step3: Open the gaps list to see what is missing and how to close it, and keep evidence up to date so the coverage stays high.
overview.why: Management system standards ask you to plan, implement and show evidence. Clauses 4 to 10 share one structure across ISO standards, so one well-kept record often serves several standards at once.

readiness.title: What requirement coverage tells you
readiness.body: The score summarises how prepared you are for an audit or a regulator's review. It only counts requirements you have marked as applicable.
readiness.step1: Look at the grey segment first: requirements nobody has started on yet.
readiness.step2: Then refresh evidence older than a year. Auditors expect records to be current.
readiness.step3: Open the standard to link evidence, or ask for a summary of what to do next.
readiness.why: ISO standards require you to monitor and evaluate your management system and review it at management level. Requirement coverage per standard is a simple input to that review.

readiness.title: How requirement coverage is calculated
readiness.s1Body: When a requirement does not apply to you, mark it as not applicable and write a short justification. It then leaves the calculation, so the score reflects what you actually have to do.
readiness.s2Body: A requirement is covered when you have confirmed at least one live record as evidence, or set the status to covered yourself. A partly covered requirement counts half.
readiness.s3Body: Evidence confirmed or updated within the last 365 days counts in full. Older evidence counts 60%, because auditors expect records to be kept up to date.
readiness.question: You cover a requirement with a procedure last reviewed two years ago. How much does it count?
readiness.explanation: It is still covered, but the evidence is older than a year, so it counts 60%. Review the procedure to make it count in full again.
